sources.display_name: Zinsmeister, Bharucha & Camilleri — gastric emptying half-time calculations (2012)
known_limitations: Literature citation backing a model assumption; the engine is not clinically calibrated.
sources.notes: PMID 22812490; backs the measurement-method direction, not ParkinSUM's selected point values.

sources.display_name: Camilleri et al. — scintigraphic gastric-emptying measurement variation (2012)
known_limitations: Healthy-participant measurement variation is not a Parkinson disease distribution or an individual confidence interval.
sources.notes: PMID 22747676; motivates only an illustrative one-way sensitivity transform.

sources.display_name: Nutt et al. — meal and LNAA effects on levodopa response (1984)
known_limitations: Small selected sample; supports direction and a reference-meal delay observation, not patient prediction or an unsupervised timing rule.
sources.notes: Primary human study used only within an explicitly heuristic educational model.

sources.display_name: Doi et al. — gastric emptying and levodopa pharmacokinetics (2012)
known_limitations: Small observational patient study; supports association between delayed emptying and later levodopa peak, not causal patient-level calibration.
sources.notes: Primary human study used for qualitative model direction only.

sources.display_name: Hardoff et al. — gastric emptying in Parkinson's disease (2001)
known_limitations: Group-level scintigraphic findings show broad variability and cannot supply an individual gastric-emptying curve.
sources.notes: Primary human study supporting variability and uncertainty boundaries.

sources.display_name: Siebner et al. — gastric emptying in medicated early Parkinson disease (2022)
known_limitations: Small preliminary cohort in early, medicated Parkinson disease; the null group result constrains universal claims but does not exclude delayed emptying in other stages or contexts.
sources.notes: Primary human null finding used to constrain disease-wide gastric-delay assumptions and surface heterogeneity.

sources.display_name: Abell et al. — standardized gastric-emptying scintigraphy consensus (2008)
known_limitations: Defines a standardized measurement protocol; it does not validate ParkinSUM's illustrative component curves.
sources.notes: Consensus measurement boundary; not a patient-specific curve calibration source.

sources.display_name: Crevoisier et al. — food effect on dual-release levodopa/benserazide (2003)
known_limitations: Healthy-volunteer, product-specific crossover study; food-effect magnitude must not be generalized to every formulation or patient.
sources.notes: Primary randomized crossover evidence used to constrain formulation-specific food-effect wording.

sources.display_name: Elashoff, Reedy, and Meyer — analysis of gastric-emptying data (1982)
known_limitations: Primary methods paper supporting comparison of empirical gastric-emptying curves; it does not establish a transportable individual parameter set or validate ParkinSUM.
sources.notes: DOI 10.1016/S0016-5085(82)80145-5; canonical power-exponential model lineage.

sources.display_name: Siegel et al. — biphasic nature of gastric emptying (1988)
known_limitations: Dual-labelled meal study in 24 healthy volunteers; meal-specific biphasic behavior and a fitted curve do not establish disease-wide or individual validity.
sources.notes: PMID 3343018; modified power-exponential solid-meal model.

sources.display_name: Hou et al. — Bayesian comparison of gastric-emptying models (2010)
known_limitations: Retrospective records with four hourly scintigraphic measurements and informative priors; relative fit does not prove universal structural choice or individual identifiability.
sources.notes: PMID 20649756; supports explicit model-choice and lag-definition uncertainty.

sources.display_name: Bürmen et al. — mathematical models of pellet gastric emptying (2009)
known_limitations: Fasting pellet profiles are dosage-form and state specific; the flexible five-parameter double-Weibull form creates substantial practical-identifiability and overfit risk with sparse observations.
sources.notes: PMID 19337822; lag-exponential, Weibull, and double-Weibull comparison.

sources.display_name: Bertoli et al. — MRI gastric-volume linear-exponential model (2023)
known_limitations: Linear-exponential fitting applies to MRI-measured absolute gastric volume with possible early secretion-related increase; it is not interchangeable with normalized tracer retention.
sources.notes: Open-access primary study used to enforce observable-and-formula coupling.

sources.display_name: Ben Guebila and Thiele — levodopa PBPK-COBRA model (2016)
known_limitations: Mechanistic research model with many parameters and some kinetic fitting to averaged fasting healthy-volunteer plasma data; it does not validate individual, fed, Parkinson-disease, brain-exposure, or motor-response predictions in ParkinSUM.
The paper's access license must not be assumed to cover every underlying code, model, or dataset artifact.
sources.notes: PMID 28725472; DOI 10.1038/npjsba.2016.13; PBPK architecture precedent only.

sources.display_name: Simon et al. — population levodopa PK/PD in peak-dose dyskinesia (2016)
known_limitations: Thirty selected patients with advanced Parkinson disease and peak-dose dyskinesia under a study-specific dose and endpoint; population variability and effect-site estimates are not individual predictions or broadly transportable parameters.
sources.notes: PMID 26936272; population PK/effect-site boundary source.

sources.display_name: EMA — PBPK modelling and simulation reporting guideline
known_limitations: Regulatory reporting guidance, not approval, qualification, clinical validation, or evidence that ParkinSUM satisfies an intended context of use.
sources.notes: Used for intended-purpose, platform, input, assumption, uncertainty, and predictive-performance reporting boundaries.

sources.display_name: FDA — assessing credibility of computational modeling and simulation
known_limitations: Risk-informed credibility guidance for a defined context of use; it is not regulatory clearance, clinical validation, or a claim that ParkinSUM meets the guidance.
sources.notes: Used to separate engineering verification from context-of-use model credibility.
